for-a-names-controller.text: Wallet change must not disable recovery or retirement. A record created by an insert fold contains exactly ADA and its representative. Maintain and recover preserve every token policy, name and quantity. ADA may increase but not decrease. The diagram follows a clean record through maintenance, recovery and custody, with an extra token causing refusal.

when-a-value-is-refused.text: Record value preservation means a continuation changed its tokens or reduced ADA. Keep wallet change separate. Record single asset identifies an invalid input shape or insert-fold output. The compiled validator retains these diagnostic names, and the runners inspect every policy. Existing polluted records remain maintainable only with unchanged tokens; under this rule they cannot be repaired, recovered or retired. An arbitrary transfer to the script address is not a registration.

deployment-compatibility.text: With this rule the application validator hash begins one two three nine f three. Before it, the hash began eight nine four zero nine eight, and that is the one the preprod record carries, because that deployment predates the rule. Spending and minting purposes share the identity, and the script identity manifest is regenerated from the pinned Aiken build. Other unapplied hashes stay the same, but the next deployment must derive addresses and applied policies from the new blueprint. The rule does not migrate records at an old script address, change an existing deployment manifest, or deploy to preprod.

checks-and-model-boundary.text: Run the record value test recipe from offchain for a positive maintenance control and named refusals against the production blueprint. These are component fixtures, not submitted transactions. Naming flake checks cover Aiken and identity; root CI covers model, simulator, browser and documentation. Lean is unchanged, and the correspondence table records the single-representative refinement.
